grh_aa56698e862ced2ef060.title: Final Fall
paragraphs: Elderly North Woods recluse Andy Fritzen, a former lumberjack of mixed Ojibwe heritage, is offered ten thousand dollars by the government for the land around his isolated cabin. Andy refuses to regard the property as his to sell, insisting that he is only its caretaker and that it belongs to his mother's people. A drinking trip during a blizzard leaves him snow-blind, hospitalized and furious at the institutions trying to manage his life; even an attempt to mail the check back ends with a brief arrest because he carries no identification. Andy finally returns the money, watches his friend Clarence prepare to marry and move away, and chooses to remain in the regrown forest, accepting his own part in having once cut it down and finding meaning in watching the land heal.

Other credited names include Fletcher Markle as director, Don Diamond as producer, Fletcher Markle as producer, Percy Grainger as writer, and Don Diamond as host.

grh_aa95ee61869f3ef5cacc.title: Too Many Crooks
paragraphs: Harry is summoned to Budapest by banker Fekity, who says his bank is about to be robbed. Harry discovers an elaborate tunnel scheme involving his old acquaintance Lulu, the Coralli gang and bank employee Fodor, but every participant plans to double-cross the others. Fekity himself intends to steal the bank's money and blame the robbers, while Lulu expects Harry to help her escape with the entire haul. Harry locks Lulu and the tunnel gang below the flower shop, then anonymously tips police to Fekity as he walks out of his own bank carrying the money. The police arrest Fekity and the gang, while Harry positions himself to collect the various rewards offered for stopping the robbery and capturing the wanted crooks.
